questions.question: Explain why the oceans and fish are important resources, with reference to South Africa.
questions.expected_answer: Oceans 71% of surface; food (protein for billions), jobs, trade, climate. Rich fishing on continental shelves and upwelling areas; food chain: phytoplankton, zooplankton, small fish, larger predators. SA: about 3 000 km coast; cold Benguela (west, upwelling, very productive) and warm Agulhas (east, more species, fewer fish). Catches: hake (trawl, most valuable), sardines/pilchards, anchovies (canned, fish meal), snoek, tuna, squid, rock lobster; jobs in small coastal towns; small-scale fishers. Fish renewable if enough adults breed.

questions.question: Explain what over-fishing is and why it happens.
questions.expected_answer: Catching fish faster than reproduction and growth replace them; adults or juveniles removed; stock shrinks and may collapse. FAO: over-fished stocks rose from about 10% (1974) to over a third. Causes: rising demand (population, health, fish meal); technology (factory ships, sonar, satellites, trawl, purse seine, longlines); shared resource (high seas beyond 200 nautical miles, tragedy of the commons); weak management, quotas too high, illegal/unreported/unregulated fishing, subsidies.

questions.question: Describe the effects of over-fishing, using Newfoundland cod and South African examples.
questions.expected_answer: Effects: smaller stocks, loss of large breeding fish, vulnerable slow-growing species; food webs disrupted (predators, prey, penguins critically endangered 2024); bycatch (dolphins, turtles, seabirds, sharks); bottom trawling damage; ghost nets; lost jobs, food, incomes, declining towns. Newfoundland: Grand Banks, factory trawlers from 1950s, 200-mile zone 1977 but quotas too high, moratorium July 1992, about 30 000-40 000 jobs lost, decades of slow recovery (ecosystem changed). SA: West Coast rock lobster severely depleted (overfishing, poaching, low-oxygen walkouts); abalone/perlemoen poached by syndicates for East Asia, fishery closed 2008; line fish (red steenbras, silver kob, seventy-four collapsed and banned), line fish emergency 2000; hake MSC certified 2004.
